newsitem.title: CHINA: China says it sincere, flexible in WTO bid.
newsitem.headline: China says it sincere, flexible in WTO bid.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it had been flexible and sincere in its bid to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) and it hoped this would gain a favourable response from the international community.
A plan to cut average import duties to 15 percent by the year 2000 after slashing them to 23 percent this year was proof of Beijing's sincerity, said Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai.
"All of this helps prove that China is sincere about joining the World Trade Organisation," Cui told reporters in a reference to the tariff cuts.
"China has demonstrated sufficient flexibility in its actions."

President Jiang Zemin, in a speech at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum at Subic Bay in the Philippines on Monday, announced the turn of the century target for the nation's import duties.
His speech was just a year after he stole the show at an APEC meeting in Japan with high-profile promises of tariff cuts that went into effect in April.
China insists it is a developing country and should be given favourable treatment in its proposal to join the global trade organisation.
The United States and other WTO members argue that China's fast-expanding financial muscle means Beijing should accept tougher entry requirements.
China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said on Monday that Beijing expects to conclude talks with the United States over joining the WTO in the first half of next year.
"China has made great efforts" to meet WTO standards, Cui said.
"We hope these efforts will gain a response from the international community."
